title: Quantitative reconstruction from finite causal orders in a conformal diamond
description:
Preprint by Daniel Eric Fredriksen, Quantyra Inc., version 0.3.0. For smooth densities on the unit square between 1/2 and 3/2, with uniform marginals and Euclidean Lipschitz constant at most two, iid finite directed causal-order laws yield the explicit coefficient inverse bound 100(N^(-1/12) + Delta_N). A logarithmic grid scale improves the sample-size term to give 130((log N/N)^(1/6) + Delta_N), for every integer N at least two.

This revision documents the completed Lean 4 formalization of the original inverse estimate and all-size identifiability for actual labeled and unlabeled directed-order laws, including normalization, concentration, cumulative reconstruction, density interpolation, transpose transport, exchangeability and exact labeled/unlabeled total variation equality. Pinned Lean 4.30.0/mathlib sources at commit b7d762acc9c10ca881f8366f545f3998b0528448 were verified on GCP with 68 selected export audits, zero compiler warnings and no added axioms or admitted proofs. The improved logarithmic-grid rate and proper-time comparison remain prose proofs.

The constants are conservative; no optimal exponent, practical sample budget, general spacetime reconstruction or new physics is claimed. Originality remains provisional, including outstanding full-text literature comparisons. Developed with OpenAI Codex assistance under the author's research direction. Quantyra follows open-source, decentralized informal feedback and downstream use/testing; specialist review is not a publication prerequisite. Manuscript and source: CC-BY-4.0. The related version 0.1.0 software DOI identifies the separate historical Apache-2.0 software release; the completed formalization is identified by its exact later source commit.
